Orbs now say which CLI they are. That is this release.

Claude, Codex, Grok and OpenClaw used to look the same from across the
room — the initials named the session, not the tool. Each local CLI orb
now wears a 22px disc in the bottom-left: terracotta spark, green star,
black X, lobster. Kind, heart and presence match that size, so an
OpenClaw channel is a lobster and an `@`, not a logo next to punctuation.

Still a beta. Codex usage is read off the last rollout on disk, the same
way Grok usage is read off its credits log: no login token, as fresh as
the last session. See *Known limitations*.

## New: CLI marks on every local orb

A Claude orb, a Codex orb, a Grok orb and an OpenClaw orb are no longer
the same circle with different letters. Bottom-left:

- **Claude** — terracotta spark
- **Codex** — green star
- **Grok** — black X
- **OpenClaw** — lobster-red lobster

Remote-control orbs skip it: those are Claude Code on another machine,
and a spark there would look like a local Claude. OpenClaw keeps the
lobster even when it also has a kind badge — kind says cron / channel /
direct, the lobster says it is OpenClaw.

Usage orbs wear the same mark.

## New: usage orbs for Codex (off by default)

Settings → **Codex sessions** now has the same usage-orb switch Claude
Code and Grok already had. Codex already writes the five-hour and weekly
windows onto every `token_count` event in the rollout; there is no
`codex usage` CLI and `/status` only exists inside a live session, so
the orb reads the newest snapshot off disk. Credits without a cap stay a
dotted inner ring rather than a share of a budget Codex did not send.

The figure is as fresh as the last Codex session on this machine —
Claude Buddy does not hold Codex's login token.

## Fix: Grok usage orbs actually appear

0.5.1 shipped the Grok usage switch. Turning it on wrote the setting and
then asked a path that still looked only at the Claude Code flag: with
that off, every account orb closed; with that on, the Grok orb waited
out a five-minute Claude poll that has nothing to do with reading a log
file. Either way the switch said true and the screen stayed empty. The
Grok orb now draws when its own switch is on.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.2-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.2-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.2-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `ClaudeBuddySpeech-0.5.2-beta-*.zip` assets are the optional high-quality
voice engine. **You do not download these yourself** — the app fetches the
right one when you turn the setting on. They are published here because that is
where it looks.

The .NET runtime is bundled; nothing else is needed. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers
every file — verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` on macOS or
`Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows.

## Upgrading from 0.5.1-beta

**macOS**: replace the app in Applications. The signing identity is unchanged,
so Automation permission and click-to-focus carry over.

**Local Network permission does not.** Replacing the app loses the grant, and
paired machines plus an OpenClaw gateway start failing with `No route to
host`. Approve it again in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local
Network. A headless Mac still cannot; pair from the machine with a screen
and add the headless one by address.

**Windows**: run the new setup over the old one; it upgrades in place and
leaves your hook configuration alone.

Codex usage orbs are off by default. Turn them on under Settings → Codex
sessions if you want them.

## Installing fresh

**macOS** — open the DMG, drag Claude Buddy to Applications, then double-click
**Install Hooks.command**. Launch from Applications; nothing appears in the
Dock and no window opens, which is correct — look in the menu bar.

**Windows** — run the setup. Per-user, so no UAC prompt. Leave the hook
checkboxes ticked; tick **"Wire hooks for Claude Code running inside WSL"**
too if you use it.

### The hook step is not optional

Claude Buddy learns about your sessions from a hook that Claude Code, Codex,
and Grok each run. Until it's wired in, the app starts and runs correctly and
shows **nothing at all**. The installers offer to wire it up; let them.
Existing settings are backed up first, and re-running repairs rather than
duplicating.

## Known limitations

Everything below is named because it was not measured, not because it is
expected to fail.

- **Windows Codex usage and Windows Grok usage have not been run** against a
  live CLI on that OS. CI runs the parse tests on both legs; a real
  `~/.codex` / `~/.grok` on Windows has not been read by the app.
- **Codex usage is as fresh as the last rollout `token_count`.** There is no
  public `codex usage` CLI, and this app does not hold Codex's token.
- **Grok usage is as fresh as the last Grok session's log line**, same as
  0.5.1.
- **Local Network consent is lost on every upgrade**, same as 0.5.1.
- **Windows installers are unsigned** — SmartScreen warns; choose **More info →
  Run anyway**. macOS builds are signed and notarized and open normally.
